transformations.name: Replace
transformations.description: Replaces every occurrence of a text with another text. The match is exact, including upper and lower case.

new.title: Replace with
new.description: Leave empty to delete every match.

text.title: Text
text.description: Added after the last character. Spaces are kept.

text.title: Text
text.description: Added before the first character. Spaces are kept.

transformations.name: Substring
transformations.description: Keeps part of the text, counting characters as you see them. Works like a Python slice: text[start:end].

start.title: Start
start.description: Position of the first character to keep, counting from 0. Negative numbers count from the end: -1 is the last character.

end.title: End
end.description: Position of the first character to leave out. Leave empty to keep everything up to the end.

transformations.name: Change case
transformations.description: Writes the text in upper, lower or title case, or turns each line into a name such as camelCase or snake_case.

to.title: Case
to.description: camelCase and the other identifier styles turn each line into one name, made of its words.

language.title: Language
language.description: Turkish and Azerbaijani have a dotted İ and a dotless ı, so i and I change differently there.

transformations.name: Line operations
transformations.description: Sorts the lines, removes duplicate or blank ones, or reverses their order.

operation.title: Operation
operation.description: Sorting puts numbers in order of their value, so line 2 comes before line 10. Removing duplicates keeps the first of them.

ignoreCase.title: Ignore case
ignoreCase.description: Treats upper and lower case as the same when sorting or finding duplicates.

transformations.name: Encode
transformations.description: Encodes the text as Base64, for a URL, or as hexadecimal digits. The text is read as UTF-8.

format.title: Format
format.description: URL encoding writes a space as %20 and keeps only letters, digits and - . _ ~ as they are.

transformations.name: Decode
transformations.description: Decodes Base64, URL encoding or hexadecimal digits back into text. The bytes must be UTF-8.

format.title: Format
format.description: Spaces and line breaks in Base64 and hexadecimal are ignored. In URL encoding, + stays a +.

transformations.name: Reformat dates
transformations.description: Reads each line as a date or time in one pattern and writes it in another. Empty lines stay empty.

from.title: Input pattern
from.description: How the dates are written now, such as yyyy-MM-dd: yyyy year, MM month, MMM month name, dd day, HH hour, mm minute. Put other text in single quotes.

to.title: Output pattern
to.description: How to write them, such as dd.MM.yyyy or d MMMM yyyy.

transformations.name: Regex extract
transformations.description: Finds the matches of a regular expression and outputs them one per line. Outputs empty text when nothing matches.

pattern.title: Pattern
pattern.description: A Java regular expression, for example \d+ for numbers.

group.title: Group
group.description: 0 outputs the whole match; 1 and up output what that pair of parentheses matched.

matches.title: Matches
matches.description: Output the first match only, or all of them.

ignoreCase.title: Ignore case
ignoreCase.description: Treats upper and lower case as the same, also for letters such as Ä and ä.

multiline.title: Multiline
multiline.description: ^ and $ match at the start and end of every line, not only of the whole text.

transformations.name: Regex replace
transformations.description: Replaces every match of a regular expression. The replacement can insert parts of the match.

pattern.title: Pattern
pattern.description: A Java regular expression, for example \d+ for numbers.

replacement.title: Replace with
replacement.description: Use $1 or ${name} to insert a group and \$ for a dollar sign. Leave empty to delete every match.

ignoreCase.title: Ignore case
ignoreCase.description: Treats upper and lower case as the same, also for letters such as Ä and ä.

multiline.title: Multiline
multiline.description: ^ and $ match at the start and end of every line, not only of the whole text.

examples.name: Find e-mail addresses
examples.input: Write to anna@example.com or bob@example.org; anna@example.com reads both.
